title: RF-DETR-S vs YOLOX-L: benchmark on one protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol at each model's default input: accuracy ties at 55.1 vs 55.4 mAP, and RF-DETR-S uses less than a third the peak VRAM.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: Accuracy is a tie: RF-DETR-S and YOLOX-L land at 55.1 vs 55.4 mAP@50-95 on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch. The two run at different input sizes, RF-DETR-S at 512 px and YOLOX-L at 640 px, each at its author default. On this GPU YOLOX-L is 16% faster, but that lead reverses on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT FP32, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. RF-DETR-S also uses far less peak VRAM at 176 vs 307 MB.

RF-DETR-S (32.11M parameters, Apache-2.0) runs at 512 px input, while YOLOX-L (54.21M, Apache-2.0) runs at 640 px. Each figure is the author default, so this is a comparison of shipped configurations, not a matched-resolution test. Both were evaluated on COCO val2017 with verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RF-DETR-S and YOLOX-L highlighted against the full set of measured models.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. RF-DETR-S measures 55.1 mAP@50-95 and YOLOX-L 55.4, close enough to call a tie. The one row that separates them is small objects: YOLOX-L leads 39.0 vs 35.1 mAP_small, a 10.01% relative gap. At 640 px, YOLOX-L keeps more small-object detail.

On the RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOX-L is 16.41% faster in PyTorch (42.8 vs 35.8 FPS). That lead does not carry. On ONNX Runtime RF-DETR-S leads 68.5 vs 50.6 FPS, on TensorRT FP32 77.5 vs 61.8 FPS, on Jetson Orin 6.9 vs 5.8 FPS, and on Raspberry Pi 5 1.0 vs 0.4 FPS.

The speed answer here is not portable. YOLOX-L wins on desktop PyTorch; RF-DETR-S is faster on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT FP32, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5. Benchmark on your own runtime before choosing.

Pick RF-DETR-S for most deployment targets: it is faster on ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, Jetson Orin, and Raspberry Pi 5, and uses less than a third the peak VRAM at 176 vs 307 MB. Pick YOLOX-L for desktop PyTorch throughput or when small-object recall at 640 px is the priority. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rfdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRFDETRs.pt") # 512 px, 55.1 mAP@50-95
yolox = LibreYOLO("LibreYOLOXl.pt")   # 640 px, 55.4 mAP@50-95

results = rfdetr("image.jpg")
